summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on PR #416, then update project documentation (DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, and a new filesystem specification) on a dedicated docs branch.
summary.outcome: All 4 review threads were triaged, fixed, replied to, and resolved; a docs branch was created with 4 files updated/created and merged as PR #419; a pending todo for web worker encryption was moved to done.

repo: cipher-box is a monorepo with apps (web, api), packages (sdk, sdk-core), crates (fuse, etc.), and tests (web-e2e, sdk-e2e, load) directories
Planning artifacts live under .planning/ with phases numbered (e.g. 37-parallel-batch-upload-pipeline), DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, STATE.md, and per-phase CONTEXT/PLAN/SUMMARY docs
Todos are tracked as markdown files under .planning/todos/pending/ and .planning/todos/done/
Integration tests in packages/sdk/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts require a live backend and are expected to fail in CI without one — these are pre-existing failures, not regressions
Web Worker encryption was implemented in phase 37 (encrypt-worker.service.ts, encrypt.worker.ts, encrypt.types.ts) but the pending todo was not moved to done until explicitly caught at end of session
Batch upload is implemented in the JS SDK and web app but NOT in the Rust SDK — the feature matrix needs to reflect per-SDK status
CipherBox filesystem enforces Windows-compatible naming rules (case-insensitive) as the strictest common denominator across Desktop OSes
FUSE mount rules and name validation constants are split between crates/fuse/src/ (helpers.rs, constants.rs, inode.rs) and sdk-core validation logic

code.finding: getWorker() and postMessage() calls could throw, leaving pending entries in the map and causing memory leaks; fixed with try/catch that deletes the pending entry on error

Batch reads all files into memory before SDK call — a known architectural limitation deferred because fixing it requires changing the SDK contract to accept File objects or read callbacks instead of Uint8Array
uploadFiles() doc comment overstated memory bounding — fixed to accurately describe actual memory behavior

workflow: Use gh api graphql with reviewThreads query to fetch all PR review threads including isResolved status; REST API does not expose thread resolution state
Reply to review threads via REST (repos/.../pulls/.../comments with in_reply_to as integer using --field not -f), then resolve via GraphQL mutation resolveReviewThread
When multiple reviewers flag the same issue (CodeRabbit + Copilot both flagged postMessage throw), treat as duplicate and apply one fix but reply/resolve both threads
156 unit tests passing with 3 pre-existing integration test failures is an acceptable baseline — document this distinction rather than blocking on it
Moving todos from pending to done should be part of the implementation commit/PR, not an afterthought — easy to miss without an explicit checklist step

friction: git push failed on first attempt for the docs branch and required a retry
Web worker encryption todo was left in pending/ after the feature shipped — required an explicit user question to catch; the review-comments workflow had no step to cross-check todos
Copilot flagged the same lazy file-read issue (useDropUpload.ts:140) that CodeRabbit had already identified and that was already tracked as a deferred item, adding noise to the review round
open_items: Lazy file reading within concurrency pool (useDropUpload.ts:140) — requires SDK contract change to accept File objects or read callbacks instead of Uint8Array; tracked in DEFERRED.md
Batch upload not implemented in the Rust SDK — feature parity gap documented in FEATURES.md matrix

~24 deferred items catalogued from phases 28-37 including: observability/structured logging improvements, upload pipeline enhancements (resumable uploads, server-sent progress events), FUSE cross-platform naming gap resolution, and infra hardening items
Five documented cross-platform filesystem gaps in FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md (case sensitivity behavior differences between macOS/Linux/Windows FUSE mounts)
E2E test coverage for desktop app likely incomplete — desktop E2E directory was checked but not fully inventoried during this session
